opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Miller (employee ID E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E017.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jennifer Miller (Analyst, full_time) requests write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write (admin only if their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security check: Jennifer Miller (E017) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; write is not permitted with basic training. Requested write exceeds the maximum allowed, so recommend read.
reason: The two memory notes for Jennifer Miller (E017) conflict on employment type: the HR note says full_time Analyst (max write for Source Code), while the Security note says contractor with basic security training (max read). Given the unresolved conflict, I apply the more restrictive interpretation: as a contractor with basic training, write is not permitted, and the maximum allowed is read. Granting read is policy-compliant under both interpretations and never exceeds the requested write level.
